findings.title: Universal graph-only iff is false at the constant rule and lacks a general converse proof
findings.status: observed counterexample plus unresolved proof obligation
findings.reasoning: At p=q=r>0 every F_C is constant regardless of attachments, contradicting the unqualified iff. The parent source shows full-domain variation does not exclude a constant restricted-menu triple. Excluding that triple still leaves a gap: Q3(d) only says a general two-terminal factor is constant iff both nontrivial eigenvalues vanish; it does not prove nonvanishing for every connected C. Components with at least three attachments and possible products of factors are not handled. Factorization alone cannot rule out cancellation. The runner's general resolution is a printed assertion, not a check.
findings.independent_evidence: independent_check.py gives TV 0 for an embeddable two-attachment path at (2,2,2) and TV 1/72 at (3,1,2). The exact equality condition derived from Q1 and positivity is that the product over C of F_C is constant over all recorded configurations.

Keep Q1, Q2, the single-site/path results for nonconstant rules, the spectral criterion, and valid exact witnesses.
